drafted_from: tool row in tools/browse-and-publish-what-my-ai-can-use/tool-rows.json, code in do-work/make-shelf-tiles.mjs, test/make-shelf-tiles.test.mjs, marketplace-kinds.json
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make Marketplace tiles with their icons from tools.json and workflows.json using my lucide-react icons folder, and write tiles.js for my page." It runs make-shelf-tiles.mjs on your computer and tells you how many tiles it made and how many have their own icon.
no_lists_because: It reads two JSON files of shelf items and an icons folder and writes a page file, so it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Save your tools and your workflows as two JSON files of {"items": [{id, kind, title, job, steps?, icon?}]} (tool:read-rows-as-marketplace-shelf-items reads them from the shelf), for example tools.json and workflows.json.
2. Run npm install lucide-react in any folder; its node_modules/lucide-react/dist/esm/icons folder is the icons input.

3. From the Workshop checkout say "Make the tiles". Your AI reads the row with tools:list and runs node tools/browse-and-publish-what-my-ai-can-use/do-work/make-shelf-tiles.mjs --tools tools.json --workflows workflows.json --icons <that icons folder> --out tiles.js.

4. Read the last JSON line: {"result": {tiles, counts, written}}. Load tiles.js in your page (it sets window.TILES; add --global NAME for another name). Items whose title reads as a machine name (an underscore, or word-word) are left out; an item without a known icon is drawn as its kind's icon (Wrench for a tool, Workflow for a workflow).

worked_examples.title: Four items become four tiles, one with its own icon
worked_examples.ask: Make tiles of my tools and workflows with their icons.
worked_examples.given: From tools/browse-and-publish-what-my-ai-can-use/test/make-shelf-tiles.test.mjs (made-up icons folder with garden-hose.mjs, wrench.mjs and workflow.mjs) and do-work/make-shelf-tiles.mjs. Command: node tools/browse-and-publish-what-my-ai-can-use/do-work/make-shelf-tiles.mjs --tools tools.json --workflows workflows.json --icons icons --out tiles.js. tools.json holds {id tool:hose, title Water the beds, job a 120-character text, icon GardenHose} and {id tool:none, title No icon of its own, job kind icon}, plus {id tool:machine, title garden-hose_list}; workflows.json holds {id workflow:season, kind workflow, title Plan a season, job steps kept, steps [sow, water]}. In the test icons folder, garden-hose draws a path and a circle and wrench draws one path.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"result":{"tiles":[{"id":"tool:hose","kind":"tool","title":"Water the beds","job":"<the job cut to 90 characters>","steps":null,"icon":"GardenHose","svg":"<path d=\"M4 4v8\"/><circle cx=\"9\" cy=\"9\" r=\"2\"/>"},{"id":"tool:none","kind":"tool","title":"No icon of its own","job":"kind icon","steps":null,"icon":"Wrench","svg":"<path d=\"M1 1h2\"/>"},{"id":"workflow:season","kind":"workflow","title":"Plan a season","job":"steps kept","steps":["sow","water"],"icon":"Workflow","svg":"<rect width=\"8\" height=\"8\" x=\"3\" y=\"3\" rx=\"2\"/>"}],"counts":{"items":3,"tools":2,"workflows":1,"own_icons":1},"written":"tiles.js"}}. tool:machine is left out (its title has an underscore), and tiles.js holds window.TILES=[...];.
